newsitem.title: UK: U.K. purchasing data shows manufacturing growing.
newsitem.headline: U.K. purchasing data shows manufacturing growing.

text.p: Britain's Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) dipped to a seasonally adjusted 52.5 percent in December from a downward revised 54.2 in November, the Chartered Institute of Purchasing and Supply (CIPS) said on Thursday.
But the figure still indicated an expansion in manufacturing for the seventh successive month as both output and employment rose to meet further improvements in order books.
A reading above 50 indicates that manufacturing is generally expanding and one below 50 that it is generally declining.

"Although order levels rose on the whole, driven by an acceleration in the rate of growth of demand for both consumer goods and capital goods, the PMI was weakened by a modest deceleration in the overall rate of growth of order books," it said.
This was due to two main factors, the CIPS said.

Firstly, the stronger pound led to weaker growth in export markets for the second month in a row. Secondly, December saw a greater incidence of deliberate destocking designed to meet year-end inventory targets.

"Stocks of purchases showed the largest monthly fall in four years as firms reduced their monthly purchases of goods to be used in the production process. As a result, producers of components...reported a deceleration in order book growth."

December also saw an easing in the rate of growth of output, reflecting deliberate destocking policies designed to meet year-end inventory targets as firms chose to restrict output growth below the rate of growth of orders.
"Stocks of finished goods showed the sharpest monthly fall for nearly three years as a consequence," the CIPS said.

Prices paid fell sharply again and have now fallen continually for 14 months. "Some upward price pressures have been reported in recent months as demand has hardened and suppliers have become busier." Suppliers' delivery times lengthened modestly for the fourth month running.
"However, these upward pressures were more than offset by the deflationary effect of sterling's strength as manufacturers benefited from cheaper imported inputs."
Employent rose modestly in December, the fifth consecutive monthly rise, as manufacturers boosted production capacity to meet future orders growth.
The PMI is based on a weighted average of seasonally adjusted measures of output, new orders, suppliers' delivery times, stocks of items purchased and employment.
